summary: omega=pi/mean(diff(peak_times)); gamma=least-squares slope of log peak magnitudes.

capability: omega=pi/mean(diff(peak_times)); gamma=least-squares slope of log peak magnitudes.
operation: fit oscillation frequency and damping from field peaks
peak times and peak magnitudes -> omega and gamma
discovery.model: Linear one-dimensional single-spatial-Fourier-mode electrons, fixed ions.
discovery.geometry: One velocity coordinate and one spatial Fourier mode.
discovery.boundary: Finite oscillatory history; peak-based fit; no global mode identification or theory claim.

identity.relation: omega=pi/mean(diff(peak_times)); gamma=least-squares slope of log peak magnitudes.
identity.definition: omega=pi/mean(diff(peak_times)); gamma=least-squares slope of log peak magnitudes.
identity.model: Linear one-dimensional single-spatial-Fourier-mode electrons, fixed ions.
identity.geometry: One velocity coordinate and one spatial Fourier mode.
identity.boundary: Finite oscillatory history; peak-based fit; no global mode identification or theory claim.
assumptions: Velocity-window truncation and recurrence are separate from temporal integration error.

inputs.name: tt
inputs.constraints: Finite strictly increasing, same shape as dEt.

inputs.name: start
inputs.description: Window start; None means 5% of actual time span.

inputs.name: end
inputs.description: Window end; None means 80% of actual time span.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Mapping peak_indices,peak_times,peak_log_magnitudes [P>=2], scalar omega,gamma,gammas; gammas aliases gamma.
outputs.shape: As described in output mapping or tuple.
outputs.constraints: Diagnostic mapping with finite fit when enough peaks are available; otherwise the declared status.

preconditions: dEt and tt are finite one-dimensional vectors with identical shape and at least two entries; tt is real and strictly increasing.
supported: Peak-spacing frequency and least-squares logarithmic damping when at least two isolated nonzero peaks are in the selected window.
excluded: Signals without two qualifying peaks and non-oscillatory/nonlinear diagnostics.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for misaligned/nonfinite vectors, non-real/non-increasing times, or fewer than two isolated nonzero peaks.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Arithmetic/type errors from NumPy operations propagate; no native process is launched.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: The peak count is a data sufficiency condition, not an iterative convergence test.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No diagnostic mapping is returned when the peak condition fails.

example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic.vlasov_poisson import vp_diagnostic
t=np.linspace(0,30,3001)
r=vp_diagnostic(np.exp(-.1*t)*np.cos(t),t)
assert abs(r["gamma"]+.1) < 1e-4
example.description: Use a damped cosine to estimate its damping rate.
example.expected: PASS: .venv/bin/python completed; the fitted gamma is within 1e-4 of -0.1.

scope: Independent reference: an analytic tone whose angular frequency is pi/(m dt) has its maxima on grid nodes, so the peak spacing is exactly m dt and both estimators become algebraic - omega = pi/mean(diff(peak_times)) and gamma is the least-squares slope of ln|E| at those nodes. The recovered values are compared against the input frequency and exponent, not against a second fit of the same data.

Implementation relation: isolated strict maxima only, restricted to the default window [t0 + 0.05 T, t0 + 0.8 T] or the caller's [start, end], at least two of them, and peak_indices counted on the (1:-1) interior; gamma and gammas carry the same value.

Test matrix: the exact analytic tone; a damped cosine with the documented window; a non-increasing time vector; a constant record with no isolated maximum; and a record with fewer than two admissible peaks, all three rejections asserted on their own channel.

Precision budget, declared before the comparison was run: 256 eps relative for the recovered angular frequency and 256 eps absolute for the recovered exponent, both algebraic on the aligned grid; 8 eps for the peak spacing.

Evidence ceiling: the estimator assumes one standing oscillation. A rotating complex exponential has no magnitude maxima at all, and a record shorter than two periods cannot support the default window.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent semidiscrete mathematical and selected scenario regressions; actual run/installed-wheel receipts are recorded separately, not inferred from test existence.
known_limitations: Finite-window rectangle rule and sampling recurrence TR=2pi/(k*dv).
Fn4 truncated density retains original coefficient and is not renormalized after cutoff.
Peak diagnostic assumes standing oscillation; rotating complex exponential has no amplitude peaks.
